classification.difficultyReason: Explain that selecting four distinct ON positions uniquely fixes the entire panel and that selection order does not create a new configuration.

content.prompt: A panel has 10 light switches in a row. Exactly 4 are ON and the remaining 6 are OFF. Explain why the number of different configurations of the panel is given by $\binom{10}{4}$.

answer.short: Choose which 4 of the 10 switch positions are ON. The other 6 are then OFF, so each selection determines exactly one configuration: $\binom{10}{4}$.
answer.worked: Each configuration is determined by the set of 4 switch positions that are ON. The remaining 6 positions must be OFF. Order of selection does not matter, so the number of configurations is the number of unordered selections of 4 positions from 10: $\binom{10}{4}$.
